records.reason: Measure m90 at 10/1 and 110.7 mg, predicted 38.25/76.12 mL. Its measured 2/1 and 5/1 outcomes showed V2 overprediction, unlike pyridyl ketone m66. This loading-matched extension tests whether the ester requires a milder solvent-response correction.

Measure m211 at 20/1 and 54.3 mg, predicted 28.85/55.21 mL. Its measured 10/1 finish was 30.88 mL after substantial acquisition-time overprediction. Keeping loading fixed tests whether the predicted weaker-solvent rise is appropriate for phenylpyridine.

Add m146 at 2/1 and 108.3 mg, predicted 14.56/26.66 mL. It fills the loading-matched gap between measured 1/1 and 10/1 anchors, locating the steep quinoline response rather than simply extending its largest endpoints.

Measure m216 at 2/1 and 109.3 mg, predicted 13.27/25.29 mL. Existing 0/1, 5/1 and 10/1 measurements constrain the surrounding response. Alongside the selected m146 point, this tests transfer across nitrogen environments while acknowledging their different recorded loading solvents.

Add m36 at 1/1 and 38.5 mg, predicted 11.31/23.78 mL. Its measured 2/1 point substantially exceeded the acquisition prediction. This stronger-solvent anchor constrains the aromatic NH2/carbonyl response; the changed sample amount prevents interpreting the comparison as a pure solvent slope.

Introduce benzylic secondary alcohol m61 at 5/1 and 101.2 mg, predicted 8.61/16.03 mL. Paired with its selected 10/1 point, it tests transfer from measured secondary-alcohol curves to an OH directly attached to the aromatic-bearing carbon.

Measure m61 at 10/1 under the same loading and injection conditions as its selected 5/1 point, predicted 13.39/24.18 mL. The modest predicted response tests OH-environment representation after larger measured responses in m60 and m67, without assuming differently recorded contexts must behave identically.

Measure tertiary alcohol m51 at 5/1 and 48.3 mg, predicted 14.88/25.66 mL. This begins a matched weak-solvent pair testing OH accessibility and aromatic spacing. Its existing 2/1 anchor is useful context but has a different sample amount.

Pair m51 at 10/1 with its selected 5/1 point at identical 48.3 mg loading, predicted 31.84/52.78 mL. The pair distinguishes the substantial predicted solvent response from a flatter tertiary-alcohol response and extends learning beyond primary and secondary alcohols.

Measure m119 at 5/1 and 158.7 mg, predicted 50.36/80.01 mL. Comparison with its measured 105.8 mg point directly tests loading at fixed injection conditions. It asks whether the large loading contrast in methoxybenzyl alcohol transfers across an extra methylene.

Measure m120 at 1/1 and 55.65 mg, predicted 10.60/17.03 mL. Its measured 166.95 mg counterpart provides a fixed-ratio loading contrast. This determines whether the striking 5/1 amount dependence is localized to that mobile phase.

Add m205 at 2/1 and 99 mg, predicted 26.72/51.21 mL. It matches the amount of a measured 1/1 anchor and supplies a same-ratio loading comparison with the measured 148.5 mg point. This separates solvent response from loading after the large 5/1 miss.

Measure m205 at 1/1 and 148.5 mg, predicted 14.62/28.98 mL. With the selected 99 mg 2/1 point and measured opposite corners, this completes a two-ratio, two-amount comparison. The existing 49.5 mg 1/1 measurement supplies another loading reference.

Measure the unobserved m81 5/1 point at 55.5 mg, predicted 5.88/14.32 mL. Its measured 111 and 166.5 mg counterparts finish at 18.57 and 9.23 mL. The prior narrative's purported low-load outcome belongs to m193 in the observed table, so this discrimination remains necessary.

Measure m125 at 2/1, 100 mg and 300 uL DCM, predicted 11.90/40.61 mL. A measured counterpart uses the same molecule, ratio and amount with 500 uL DCM. This directly isolates recorded injection volume, resolving a confound in earlier loading comparisons.

Measure m173 at 1/1 with 1500 uL DCM, predicted 8.29/107.29 mL. The measured 2000 uL counterpart has 6.51/108.89 mL endpoints, with only 0.05 mg difference in sample amount. This near-matched volume contrast tests persistence of its unusually long interval.

Pair m173 at 2/1 with its selected 1/1 point using the same 124.75 mg and 1500 uL DCM, predicted 10.08/47.17 mL. Near-matched measured 2000 uL counterparts allow ratio dependence and injection context to be examined separately.

Measure m73 at 1/1 and 52.45 mg, predicted 14.11/19.90 mL. Its higher-load observation has unusual 18.60/18.96 mL endpoints. This controlled amount contrast tests whether m73 resembles the loading-local behavior found for m76, rather than extending the ester anomaly by analogy.

Measure m73 at 2/1 and approximately 104.91 mg, predicted 8.40/11.51 mL. Relative to its exceptional measured 1/1 observation, loading solvent and volume are unchanged and sample amount differs by only 0.01 mg. This tests whether the response is localized at 1/1.

Fill m94's 10/1 gap at 117.4 mg, predicted 30.78/62.48 mL. Matched measured 5/1 and 20/1 endpoints are 12.33/26.02 and 37.25/79.67 mL. This locates the steep cyclopropyl beta-ketoester transition after a large acquisition-time underprediction.

Extend alpha-hydroxy ester m99 to 10/1 at the same 100 mg and 1000 uL DCM as its measured 2/1 and 5/1 points. The current 22.46/39.57 mL prediction rises moderately from the measured 5/1 result, testing transfer beyond its new anchors.

Introduce acetylfluorene m38 at 5/1 and 100 mg, predicted 6.79/21.78 mL, as the baseline of a matched pair. Its observed-chemistry similarity is 0.471. It tests fused-ring topology and carbonyl placement beyond the newly measured acetylnaphthalene curve.

Pair m38 at 20/1 with its selected 5/1 point at identical loading, predicted 14.20/35.89 mL. This tests whether onset and finish move together as predicted and whether fused aromatic shape transfers from measured ketones without a common carbonyl-family correction.

Introduce methyl-substituted fused cyclic ketone m63 at 5/1 and 107.8 mg, predicted 6.58/14.49 mL. Its observed-chemistry similarity is 0.394. The matched pair connects an uncovered ring environment to measured tetralone and related cyclic-ketone families.

Measure m63 at 10/1 with the same loading as its selected 5/1 point, predicted 7.64/18.00 mL. The predicted response remains modest; measurement tests whether ring substitution and carbonyl accessibility support that behavior relative to measured cyclic-ketone responses.

Introduce phenoxyethyl acrylate m21 at 5/1 and 165.6 mg, predicted 6.22/15.19 mL. This uncovered aromatic-ether/ester combination connects the acrylate and ether families. It anchors a matched response test at moderate predicted retention.

Pair m21 at 20/1 with its selected 5/1 point at identical loading and injection conditions, predicted 9.48/20.44 mL. The pair tests the modest predicted response of the combined ether/ester environment and broadens condition learning beyond repeatedly sampled aromatic carbonyl failures.

Introduce benzyl phenyl ketone m171 at 5/1 and 120 mg, predicted 7.12/15.45 mL. Inserting a methylene relative to benzophenone changes conjugation and geometry. A matched pair tests transfer of aromatic-ketone corrections to this uncovered structural environment.

Measure m171 at 20/1 under the same loading conditions as its selected 5/1 point, predicted 7.82/16.90 mL. The nearly flat predicted response contrasts with measured methoxybenzophenone, while other measured low-retention aromatic ketones caution against assuming all two-ring ketones elute late.

Extend m40 to 50/1 at 112 mg, predicted 33.06/57.23 mL. Its matched measured 10/1 and 20/1 outcomes showed a smoother onset increase than originally predicted. This tests weak-solvent extrapolation for a simple fused aromatic ketone.

Measure conjugated ketone m164 at 50/1 and 104.77 mg, predicted 15.87/50.05 mL. Its matched measured 10/1 and 20/1 points separate an initially stable onset from a later onset shift. This tests endpoint-specific extrapolation across conjugated carbonyl structures.

Obtain a near-replicate of m73's exceptional 1/1 observation, predicted 14.11/19.91 mL. Recorded conditions match except for a density difference yielding 0.01 mg extra sample. Together with the lower-load and 2/1 selections, it distinguishes reproducibility, amount dependence and ratio locality.

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing scaffolds require distinct solvent-response relationships: the m66 pyridyl-ketone correction does not transfer uniformly to pyridyl esters, phenylpyridines, quinolines or aromatic amino ketones.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Opposite acquisition-time error directions across nitrogen environments argue against a shared upward retention adjustment. Intermediate and extended curves can teach structure-condition interactions for both endpoints.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m90 and m211 retain their milder response at weaker eluent, and where do the m146/m216 curves begin rising between their strong-solvent and 5/1 anchors?

hypotheses.content: Alcohol solvent response depends on OH environment, aromatic spacing and neighboring functional groups. The earlier predicted m205 plateau is contradicted by its loading-matched 1/1-to-5/1 measurements.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: New benzylic-secondary and tertiary-alcohol pairs test structural transfer, while extending m99 tests whether two new labels adequately constrain its OH-plus-ester response. Comparisons retain recorded injection context rather than treating HBD count as sufficient.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m61 and m51 follow their different predicted 5/1-to-10/1 slopes, and does m99 continue rising more steeply than its current prediction?

hypotheses.content: Loading dependence is scaffold- and condition-specific; large matched contrasts cannot be represented reliably by a universal loading slope, and some may reflect isolated observations or missing context.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched contrasts can establish when the density-times-volume feature helps. m81's loading contrast changes greatly between 5/1 and 10/1, while m120 and m205 show different loading directions in their measured contexts.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m81's missing low-load 5/1 label clarify its nonmonotonic finish pattern, does m120's contrast persist at 1/1, and do the m205 and m119 comparisons support transferable loading interactions?

hypotheses.content: Recorded DCM injection volume may contribute to unusual endpoint patterns in m125 and m173, but existing comparisons do not establish this effect independently of loading or other context.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A direct volume contrast for m125 and a near-matched ratio-by-volume comparison for m173 can distinguish an informative recorded feature from unexplained variation. Expectations about injection focusing remain chemical priors until tested.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed m125 amount and ratio, does changing DCM from 500 to 300 uL change the endpoints, and does m173's unusual 1/1 finish persist at both injection volumes?

hypotheses.content: The proposal that exceptional 1/1 ester endpoints transfer to close ester analogs is weakened. Reproducibility and locality of the m73 observation remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Lower-load m76, neighboring-ratio m76 and methyl analog m93 all eluted much earlier than their acquisition predictions. A near-repeat, loading contrast and neighboring-ratio measurement for m73 can prevent an isolated anomaly from imposing an inappropriate correction across many ester rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m73 reproduce its late, nearly coincident 1/1 endpoints near 104.9 mg, do they persist at half loading, and are they absent at 2/1?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl topology and recorded conditions determine whether solvent weakening shifts onset, finish or both. Carbonyl count and acceptor-richness alone do not explain the different responses of beta-ketoesters, aryldiketones and aromatic monoketones.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: m94 moves both endpoints strongly, while m166/m167 retain early onset even at 50/1. Curve gaps, extrapolation checks and matched novel-scaffold pairs can teach endpoint-specific structural response instead of a blanket polarity adjustment.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does m94's rise occur, do the modest m63 and flat m171 predicted responses hold, and do m38, m40 and m164 follow their predicted endpoint trajectories?

feedback_interpretation: The latest measurements strengthen scaffold-specific reasoning and weaken shared corrections. At acquisition time, m90 V2 was overpredicted by 10.96 mL at 2/1 and 27.04 mL at 5/1, whereas m66's new 2/1 V2 remained underpredicted by 10.00 mL. m211 at 10/1 also overpredicted V2 by 14.96 mL, while m36 at 2/1 underpredicted it by 19.60 mL. These outcomes favor distinct nitrogen-environment curves. For alcohols, the m205 plateau hypothesis is rejected: at the same 49.5 mg loading, measured endpoints increased from 10.51/25.36 mL at 1/1 to 54.52/89.72 mL at 5/1. m119 and m99 also required substantial upward acquisition-time corrections at 5/1, while m60's 10/1 prediction was close. Loading remains worth testing selectively, without assigning every miss to sample amount. The observed table assigns the outcome previously described as low-load m81 to m193 at 0/1; it therefore supplies no measured evidence for the missing m81 condition. The m76 lower-load and 2/1 results and m93 1/1 result all showed early elution, weakening transfer of the exceptional ester pattern. m73 remains a separate unresolved case. Finally, m94's large underprediction and m166/m167's overpredictions further weaken a blanket acceptor-rich upward correction. These error statements concern acquisition-time predictions, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch uses local experiments where contrasts can teach relationships that single large-error labels cannot. Nitrogen curve extensions test transfer after errors of opposite signs. Alcohol pairs explore donor environment, while matched loading comparisons and the m205 two-ratio/two-amount grid test selective use of loading information. The m125 and m173 experiments examine recorded injection volume without inventing concentration, flow or other absent variables. Three m73 experiments address reproducibility and locality of an observation that could otherwise influence a large ester family. Carbonyl curve gaps and extrapolation checks repair known transfer weaknesses, and matched novel-scaffold pairs add coverage of ring geometry, conjugation and combined ether/ester functionality. Moderate-retention and predicted-flat curves provide discriminating comparisons alongside steep-response cases. The only deliberate near-repeat is the justified m73 reproducibility test. Together, these labels may improve endpoint-specific structure-condition representations across the Row-distribution while allowing unusual observations to remain unexplained when recorded variables are insufficient.
